mainEntity.name: How should employers evaluate recruitment agencies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use consistent criteria covering relevant experience, sourcing, process, communication, costs and compliance.

mainEntity.name: Can agencies be compared using weighted scores?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Weighted criteria can support comparison when scoring rules are clearly defined and weights total 100%.

mainEntity.name: Should price be the main selection factor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Employers should consider service suitability, process quality and contractual responsibilities.

mainEntity.name: Can the scorecard support bulk recruitment vendor selection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Employers can adapt the criteria to high-volume or multi-location hiring requirements.

@graph.name: How to use a recruitment agency evaluation scorecard
@graph.description: Structured workflow for comparing recruitment providers using weighted criteria and due diligence.

step.name: Define your hiring needs
step.text: Document role categories, hiring volumes, locations and expected timelines.

step.name: Select evaluation criteria
step.text: Choose the factors most relevant to the organization.

step.name: Assign weights
step.text: For example, role expertise may carry more weight than presentation quality.

step.name: Score each provider
step.text: Use a consistent rating scale with supporting notes.

step.name: Compare results
step.text: Review weighted scores alongside commercial and operational considerations.

step.name: Complete due diligence
step.text: Verify relevant claims, references, legal terms and responsibilities before signing.
